1.title: An update id is committed once: a retry after a lost answer gets the same seq from its receipt and writes nothing.

2.title: Every acknowledged update survives a backend outage that outlasts the retry deadline and a SIGKILL of all hubs.

3.title: Unrelated updates saved on two hubs at once are all in the state rebuilt from the log.

4.title: An append committed after the compaction lease read the log survives the publication of the checkpoint, payload and pending marker included.

5.title: Of two publications of the same checkpoint range exactly one commits; the other is refused and deletes nothing.

6.title: Receipts outlive the compaction of their payloads and live as long as their generation.

7.title: Only the document's current generation takes appends; a restore between load and append refuses the old one.

8.title: A writer rechecked to read-only cannot write through any path but keeps receiving; a reader rechecked to none is closed.

9.title: Without a control message the hub renews the token before it expires and closes the connection when the renewal is refused.

10.title: SIGTERM while a client types: readiness falls at once, health stays observable, nothing is saved after the drain boundary.

11.title: Where an update comes from decides who appends it: server changes once, Redis-relayed changes never, client envelopes once.

12.title: Switching the module off (managed drain, raw disable, uninstall) never discards edits that live only in the log.

13.title: A restore closes the generation it leaves: no append, lease or checkpoint of that generation is accepted afterwards.

14.title: Client protocol 2: an envelope is acknowledged only after the commit, and its repeat is byte-identical.

15.title: Control message lost and the backend unreachable: the token expiry closes the connection within the clock skew.

16.title: A failed append is kept and repeated by the next flush cycle without a new change.

17.title: The append refuses what it cannot take (size, hash, payload limits) before it allocates or writes.

18.title: A restore or replace of a document with uncheckpointed edits first drains them through the hub.

19.title: The compaction lease is handed out only for the current, open generation that reached a trigger or a drain request.

20.title: While a pending marker stays, a REST replace answers 409 document_state_pending.
